title: Cache stampede: when one TTL expires and 10000 requests hit the DB
summary: Why a single TTL expiry turns a hot cache key into a flash DDoS against the origin, and the four mechanisms — locks, single-flight, probabilistic early expiration, and stale-while-revalidate — that keep the database alive.
crux: One TTL expires. 10000 requests miss at once. The DB sees flash-DDoS from its own cache. Four fixes: lock, single-flight, XFetch, SWR.
keytakeaway: Cache stampede = TTL boundary + concurrency. Fix with lock, single-flight, XFetch, SWR — composed in layers. Each tier collapses the herd by an order of magnitude.
